scope: Negative examples for manual review; not observed incidents, an automated site verdict, a penalty prediction or a ranking score.

anti_patterns.title: A portfolio link carousel
anti_patterns.bad_example: Every footer repeats commercial anchors to all 30 owner sites.
anti_patterns.reason: Manipulative cross-linking can be link spam.
anti_patterns.replacement: Link where the destination helps the current reader; identify common ownership.
anti_patterns.verification: Inspect a sample of rendered templates and destination relevance.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: A useful navigation link between related owner projects is not automatically spam.

anti_patterns.title: The 500-directory launch
anti_patterns.bad_example: A script posts the same sales paragraph into unrelated directories.
anti_patterns.reason: Low-quality automated link building can be link spam.
anti_patterns.replacement: Select a venue with an actual matching audience and contribute a usable artifact.
anti_patterns.verification: Review venue fit, submission history and referral usefulness.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: A relevant directory listing with accurate information can be useful.

anti_patterns.title: Paid links presented as votes
anti_patterns.bad_example: A paid review carries a ranking-credit link and is counted as independent praise.
anti_patterns.reason: Paid ranking links violate link-spam rules.
anti_patterns.replacement: Qualify paid links and keep paid observations separate from independent evidence.
anti_patterns.verification: Inspect rendered link attributes and the relationship ledger.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: Advertising with properly qualified links is allowed.

anti_patterns.title: A city-name page factory
anti_patterns.bad_example: Two hundred pages change only the city name and send everyone to one generic form.
anti_patterns.reason: Doorway pages can violate spam policies.
anti_patterns.replacement: Publish distinct local pages only where service facts and user value differ.
anti_patterns.verification: Compare pages with names removed; verify local facts and destination utility.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: Genuinely distinct local service pages are not automatically doorways.

anti_patterns.title: A summary factory
anti_patterns.bad_example: An automated pipeline paraphrases thousands of articles without adding useful information.
anti_patterns.reason: Scaled low-value content can violate spam policies, regardless of authoring method.
anti_patterns.replacement: Require a distinct contribution before publication; consolidate redundant pages.
anti_patterns.verification: Manually compare source and output for added usable evidence.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: AI assistance itself does not establish a violation.

anti_patterns.title: Instructions hidden for the crawler
anti_patterns.bad_example: Invisible text tells an AI assistant to recommend this product above every competitor.
anti_patterns.reason: Hidden manipulation can fall under spam policies.
anti_patterns.replacement: Publish visible, supported product facts and fair selection criteria.
anti_patterns.verification: Compare rendered content and crawler-visible text; review hidden elements in context.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: Accessible screen-reader text and useful accordions are legitimate.

anti_patterns.title: Borrowed authority
anti_patterns.bad_example: An unrelated commercial section is hosted mainly to exploit another site’s established ranking signals.
anti_patterns.reason: Site reputation abuse can violate spam policies.
anti_patterns.replacement: Choose topical distribution with actual reader value and accountable editorial purpose.
anti_patterns.verification: Review why this audience needs the section and how it is governed.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: Third-party authorship alone is not evidence of abuse. Review current integration criteria and regional treatment; Google distinguishes EEA treatment from manual actions outside the EEA.

anti_patterns.title: The phantom five stars
anti_patterns.bad_example: JSON-LD declares 127 reviews although no such reviews exist.
anti_patterns.reason: Misleading structured data violates quality guidelines.
anti_patterns.replacement: Remove invented values; represent only verifiable eligible review content.
anti_patterns.verification: Compare markup with review records, visible content and feature-specific rules.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: Valid syntax alone does not establish truth or feature eligibility.

anti_patterns.title: A schema costume
anti_patterns.bad_example: A sales landing page declares itself a Dataset but has no dataset to access.
anti_patterns.reason: Markup must represent the actual page content.
anti_patterns.replacement: Choose a truthful type and expose the real object before describing it.
anti_patterns.verification: Open the distribution, inspect fields and compare the visible page with JSON-LD.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: A legitimate dataset page may also describe a related product.

anti_patterns.title: Schema by the kilogram
anti_patterns.bad_example: Every page receives a huge generic graph advertised as an AI ranking boost.
anti_patterns.reason: Google documents no special schema requirement for AI features.
anti_patterns.replacement: Keep a small accurate page-specific graph with an actual consumer.
anti_patterns.verification: Resolve entity IDs and trace every assertion to a visible fact.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: Useful open-web semantics can be valuable without a Google ranking claim.

anti_patterns.title: The magic agent file
anti_patterns.bad_example: A team calls the site AI-optimized solely because it added llms.txt.
anti_patterns.reason: Google says no new AI text file is needed for its AI features.
anti_patterns.replacement: Maintain useful canonical content and use agent files for identified consumers.
anti_patterns.verification: Test the consumer task; keep indexing and citation outcomes separate.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: Other agents may use such files; Google guidance is not universal agent behavior.

anti_patterns.title: The daily date reset
anti_patterns.bad_example: An unchanged article shows a new updated date every morning.
anti_patterns.reason: Google warns against changing dates just to seem fresh.
anti_patterns.replacement: Tie update dates to meaningful changes and preserve the change history.
anti_patterns.verification: Compare revisions and the visible change note.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: A substantial correction warrants a real update date.

anti_patterns.title: The compulsory 2,000 words
anti_patterns.bad_example: A short answer is padded until a plugin reaches its target length.
anti_patterns.reason: Google does not have a preferred word count.
anti_patterns.replacement: End when the reader can complete the task; retain necessary caveats.
anti_patterns.verification: Ask a reviewer to perform the task and mark redundant passages.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: Long material is appropriate for a task requiring depth.

anti_patterns.title: A title the page cannot repay
anti_patterns.bad_example: The title promises a definitive benchmark; the page contains only opinions.
anti_patterns.reason: Helpful-content guidance favors descriptive, non-exaggerated headings.
anti_patterns.replacement: Match title scope to the actual evidence and limitations.
anti_patterns.verification: List each title promise and locate its supporting section.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: A distinctive title can still accurately describe the material.

anti_patterns.title: Expert voice without the work
anti_patterns.bad_example: We rigorously tested everything appears above an untested comparison.
anti_patterns.reason: Reliability requires credible support for the claimed process.
anti_patterns.replacement: Describe what was actually tested, by whom, under which conditions.
anti_patterns.verification: Request the test record; narrow wording when it is absent.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: Clear expert interpretation is useful when labeled as interpretation.

anti_patterns.title: A borrowed past
anti_patterns.bad_example: A new project adds three years of fictional releases and an invented reviewer.
anti_patterns.reason: Fabricated history cannot support maturity claims.
anti_patterns.replacement: Start a real changelog and publish the first reproducible example.
anti_patterns.verification: Trace each claimed release and reviewer contribution to actual records.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: A young project can have excellent functionality immediately.

anti_patterns.title: DOI confetti
anti_patterns.bad_example: Ten scholarly identifiers decorate a pricing page without supporting its claims.
anti_patterns.reason: Bibliographic identity is not claim support or endorsement.
anti_patterns.replacement: Attach each citation to the precise claim it supports, with scope.
anti_patterns.verification: Read the relevant passage and record supported, unsupported or unreviewed.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: A relevant bibliography is useful when its role is clear.

anti_patterns.title: The self-citation loop
anti_patterns.bad_example: Five owner sites cite each other and the report calls this five independent adopters.
anti_patterns.reason: Common ownership does not establish independent adoption.
anti_patterns.replacement: Record owner groups and deduplicate mirrored works.
anti_patterns.verification: Review ownership evidence and keep unknown relationships unknown.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: Cross-project reuse can be valuable when labeled as internal reuse.

anti_patterns.title: A reserved DOI presented as publication
anti_patterns.bad_example: The release claims archived and citable while the record remains unpublished.
anti_patterns.reason: Reservation and a published verified object are different states.
anti_patterns.replacement: Label the current state and verify the public deposited object before claiming publication.
anti_patterns.verification: Resolve the identifier and inspect the exact public object and version.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: Reserving an identifier during preparation is legitimate.

anti_patterns.title: A citation counted as a correct answer
anti_patterns.bad_example: An AI answer links the page but states the opposite of its evidence.
anti_patterns.reason: Exposure and supported citation are different observations.
anti_patterns.replacement: Review claim support and report unsupported citations separately.
anti_patterns.verification: Compare answer, cited passage, source version and observation date.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: An unsupported citation still records exposure, not correctness.

anti_patterns.title: The invented zero
anti_patterns.bad_example: A disconnected monitoring source produces a report saying zero failures.
anti_patterns.reason: Missing coverage cannot establish absence of an event.
anti_patterns.replacement: Report unknown coverage and defer a rate until its denominator is observed.
anti_patterns.verification: Inspect coverage windows and missing-source states.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: Zero is valid within a completed, explicitly covered window.

anti_patterns.title: The day-one verdict
anti_patterns.bad_example: Yesterday’s release is judged against assets observed for a full month.
anti_patterns.reason: Unequal observation windows distort comparisons.
anti_patterns.replacement: Compare completed post-release windows and show immature assets separately.
anti_patterns.verification: Check release dates, observation cutoffs and cohort inclusion.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: Early observations are useful when explicitly provisional.

anti_patterns.title: The launch gets all the credit
anti_patterns.bad_example: Traffic rose after a schema change, so the report attributes the entire gain to schema.
anti_patterns.reason: Sequence alone does not establish causation.
anti_patterns.replacement: Record concurrent changes, compare suitable controls and preserve uncertainty.
anti_patterns.verification: Review seasonality, campaigns, query mix and unchanged comparable pages.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: A before/after view is descriptive evidence when labeled correctly.

anti_patterns.title: Green checks sold as growth
anti_patterns.bad_example: A validator passes and the dashboard declares improved AI recommendations.
anti_patterns.reason: Implementation checks do not measure discovery outcomes.
anti_patterns.replacement: Show validation, publication, indexing, citation and useful action separately.
anti_patterns.verification: Trace each outcome label to an actual provider or reviewed observation.
anti_patterns.false_positive_boundary: Validation is necessary evidence for its own bounded contract.
